01-01.title: Mary, Mother of God
01-01.line: Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart.
01-01.meaning: the year opens with Mary, who held what she didn't yet understand. you can carry this new year the same way, one quiet day at a time.
01-01.source: Luke 2:19 (Douay-Rheims); Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God

01-02.title: Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen
01-02.line: we were one soul in two bodies.
01-02.meaning: Gregory said this of his friend Basil. two bishops and theologians, and also simply good friends. today is a nice day to thank a friend who shaped your faith.

01-03.title: The Most Holy Name of Jesus
01-03.line: at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.
01-03.meaning: a name is how we call someone close. saying his name slowly, once, can be a whole prayer.

01-04.title: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton
01-04.line: she turned loss into schools that still teach today.
01-04.meaning: a widow and mother of five, she became the first U.S.-born saint and started Catholic schools for children who had little. small beginnings can last a long time.

01-05.title: St. John Neumann
01-05.line: he learned new languages so families could hear God in their own.
01-05.meaning: a bishop of Philadelphia who walked his parishes and built schools for immigrant children. care often looks like learning someone else's language.

01-06.title: The Epiphany of the Lord
01-06.line: they saw the star and rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
01-06.meaning: the wise men followed a light from far away. what small light is leading you this week?
01-06.source: Matthew 2:10; traditional date of Epiphany (in the U.S. kept on a Sunday)

01-07.title: St. Raymond of Penyafort
01-07.line: he put the Church's laws in order so mercy could be found.
01-07.meaning: a Dominican scholar who lived to nearly a hundred. patient, careful work is a kind of love too.

01-08.title: Psalm 46
01-08.line: be still and see that I am God.
01-08.meaning: stillness isn't empty. it's where we notice God was here all along.

01-09.title: St. Augustine
01-09.line: our heart is restless until it rests in you.
01-09.meaning: that restless feeling isn't a flaw. it's a sign we were made for God.

01-10.title: The Our Father
01-10.line: give us this day our daily bread.
01-10.meaning: just today's bread. not next month's. enough for today is a gift.

01-11.title: Psalm 23
01-11.line: the Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.
01-11.meaning: the old Douay wording of 'the Lord is my shepherd.' you are being led and cared for.

01-12.title: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
01-12.line: prayer is a surge of the heart, a simple look turned toward heaven.
01-12.meaning: prayer doesn't need fancy words. a glance of love counts.
01-12.source: Thérèse of Lisieux, Story of a Soul (paraphrase); quoted in Catechism 2558

01-13.title: St. Hilary of Poitiers
01-13.line: he wrote twelve books on the Trinity while far from home.
01-13.meaning: a bishop sent into exile who used that time to think and write. hard seasons can still be fruitful ones.
01-13.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

01-14.title: Matthew 11
01-14.line: come to me, all you that labour, and are burdened, and I will refresh you.
01-14.meaning: if today feels heavy, this is an invitation, not a task.

01-15.title: The Glory Be
01-15.line: glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
01-15.meaning: the shortest prayer in the rosary. say it once when something good happens today.

01-16.title: John 14
01-16.line: let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid.
01-16.meaning: Jesus said this the night before he died. peace is his gift, even in hard hours.

01-17.title: St. Anthony, Abbot
01-17.line: go, sell what thou hast, and give to the poor.
01-17.meaning: Anthony heard this Gospel in church and went to the desert to pray. one verse, taken to heart, can change a whole life.

01-18.title: Brother Lawrence
01-18.line: God is as near in the kitchen as in church.
01-18.meaning: a Carmelite cook who found prayer among the pots and pans. your chores can be prayer too.
01-18.source: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God (paraphrase)

01-19.title: Luke 1
01-19.line: no word shall be impossible with God.
01-19.meaning: the angel's words to Mary. whatever feels stuck today, God is not stuck.

01-20.title: Sts. Fabian and Sebastian
01-20.line: two martyrs of Rome, remembered together for steady courage.
01-20.meaning: Fabian was a pope and Sebastian a soldier. different callings, the same faithfulness.

01-21.title: St. Agnes
01-21.line: young in years, strong in faith.
01-21.meaning: Agnes was a girl of Rome who gave her life for Christ. courage doesn't wait until we're older.
01-21.source: General Roman Calendar, memorial; Ambrose, On Virgins I.2

01-22.title: St. Vincent, deacon
01-22.line: a deacon who served the bishop and the poor of Spain.
01-22.meaning: Vincent was a martyr of Zaragoza, honored across the early Church. serving quietly beside someone is holy work.

01-23.title: The Jesus Prayer
01-23.line: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me.
01-23.meaning: an old prayer of the Eastern Church said with the breath. try it a few times, slowly.

01-24.title: St. Francis de Sales
01-24.line: have patience with all things, but first of all with yourself.
01-24.meaning: a gentle bishop who taught that holiness belongs in ordinary lives. be as kind to yourself today as you would be to a friend.

01-25.title: The Conversion of St. Paul
01-25.line: Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?
01-25.meaning: Paul's whole life turned on one honest question. it is still a good prayer to start a day with.

01-26.title: Sts. Timothy and Titus
01-26.line: let no man despise thy youth.
01-26.meaning: Paul trusted two young helpers to lead churches. someone is ready for more trust than we think.

01-27.title: St. Angela Merici
01-27.line: she gathered women to teach girls in their own homes.
01-27.meaning: Angela founded the Ursulines, first without convents or habits. you can begin good work right where you are.

01-28.title: St. Thomas Aquinas
01-28.line: grace does not destroy nature but perfects it.
01-28.meaning: the great teacher of the Church believed faith and reason are friends. your questions are welcome on the way to God.
01-28.source: Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I, q.1, a.8 (paraphrase)

01-29.title: Psalm 118
01-29.line: this is the day which the Lord hath made: let us be glad and rejoice therein.
01-29.meaning: not yesterday, not tomorrow. this one.

01-30.title: St. Francis de Sales
01-30.line: do not lose your inner peace for anything whatsoever.
01-30.meaning: the gentle bishop's advice for busy lives. peace first, then the rest.

01-31.title: St. John Bosco
01-31.line: reason, faith and kindness: that was his way with young people.
01-31.meaning: Don Bosco ran schools and workshops for street boys in Turin. he won hearts with warmth, not fear.

02-01.title: Romans 8
02-01.line: to them that love God, all things work together unto good.
02-01.meaning: even the parts of today that don't make sense yet.

02-02.title: The Presentation of the Lord
02-02.line: a light to the revelation of the Gentiles.
02-02.meaning: old Simeon waited his whole life and finally held the child. today, called Candlemas, candles are blessed for the year.

02-03.title: St. Blaise
02-03.line: today many receive the blessing of the throats with two crossed candles.
02-03.meaning: Blaise was a bishop and martyr in Armenia. a simple blessing, asked for with trust, is a good gift.
02-03.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; also St. Ansgar

02-04.title: The Hail Mary
02-04.line: holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners.
02-04.meaning: we ask Mary to pray with us, now and always. you don't pray alone.

02-05.title: St. Agatha
02-05.line: a young martyr of Sicily, loved for her quiet courage.
02-05.meaning: Agatha is remembered in the oldest prayer of the Mass, the Roman Canon. faith can stay steady under pressure.
02-05.source: General Roman Calendar, memorial; Roman Canon

02-06.title: St. Paul Miki and Companions
02-06.meaning: Paul Miki and 25 companions were martyred in Nagasaki in 1597. he forgave those who killed him.

02-07.title: Philippians 4
02-07.line: rejoice in the Lord always; again, I say, rejoice.
02-07.meaning: Paul wrote this from prison. joy can live under hard things.

02-08.title: St. Josephine Bakhita
02-08.line: she knew slavery and still chose freedom, peace and forgiveness.
02-08.meaning: kidnapped as a child in Sudan, she later became a Canossian sister in Italy, known for her gentleness. a wounded past is not the end of the story.

02-09.title: St. Ignatius of Loyola
02-09.line: take, Lord, and receive all my liberty.
02-09.meaning: the start of the Suscipe, a prayer of total trust. hold today with open hands.

02-10.title: St. Scholastica
02-10.line: she could do more, because she loved more.
02-10.meaning: Scholastica asked her brother Benedict to stay and talk of God. a storm came and kept him there.

02-11.title: Our Lady of Lourdes
02-11.line: the lady asked for prayer and for a chapel to be built.
02-11.meaning: in 1858 Mary appeared to young Bernadette at Lourdes. today is also the World Day of the Sick: pray for someone who is unwell.
02-11.source: optional memorial; World Day of the Sick

02-12.title: Isaiah 43
02-12.line: fear not, for I have redeemed thee, and called thee by thy name: thou art mine.
02-12.meaning: God knows your name. you belong.

02-13.title: 1 Corinthians 13
02-13.meaning: St. Paul's famous words on love. pick one: patient or kind, and practice it today.

02-14.title: Sts. Cyril and Methodius
02-14.line: they gave the Slavic peoples an alphabet so they could pray in their own words.
02-14.meaning: two brothers from Thessalonica, now patrons of Europe. faith spreads best in a heart's own language.

02-15.title: St. Teresa of Ávila
02-15.line: prayer is nothing but friendly talk with one who loves us.
02-15.meaning: talk to God today like you would a close friend.

02-16.title: Psalm 51
02-16.line: create a clean heart in me, O God.
02-16.meaning: a fresh start is always available.

02-17.title: The Seven Holy Founders of the Servites
02-17.line: seven friends who left business to serve Mary together.
02-17.meaning: merchants of Florence who founded the Servants of Mary. faith is easier shared.

02-18.title: The Sign of the Cross
02-18.line: in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
02-18.meaning: the simplest Catholic prayer. begin and end today with it.

02-19.title: Matthew 5
02-19.line: blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
02-19.meaning: mercy has a way of coming back around.

02-20.title: St. Catherine of Siena
02-20.line: nothing great is ever done without much patience.
02-20.meaning: slow is not failing. keep going.

02-21.title: St. Peter Damian
02-21.line: a hermit who loved quiet, called to help reform the Church.
02-21.meaning: Peter Damian loved solitude and wrote about prayer. sometimes we are asked to step out of our quiet to help.
02-21.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

02-22.title: The Chair of St. Peter
02-22.line: thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.
02-22.meaning: today honors Peter's teaching role. Jesus built on a man who had stumbled, which is good news for all of us.

02-23.title: St. Polycarp
02-23.line: eighty-six years I have served him, and he never did me wrong.
02-23.meaning: an old bishop of Smyrna who knew people who knew the apostles. long faithfulness has its own quiet beauty.

02-24.title: John 15
02-24.line: abide in me, and I in you.
02-24.meaning: Jesus compares us to branches on a vine. stay close, and growth comes.

02-25.title: Lamentations 3
02-25.line: his mercies are new every morning.
02-25.meaning: today is a new start, written right into the morning.

02-26.title: Zephaniah 3
02-26.line: he will rejoice over thee with gladness.
02-26.meaning: God isn't just patient with you. God is glad about you.

02-27.title: St. Gregory of Narek
02-27.line: an Armenian monk who wrote a whole book of prayers from the heart.
02-27.meaning: his Book of Lamentations speaks to God with deep honesty. you can pray exactly as you are.
02-27.source: optional memorial (added 2021); Doctor of the Church

02-28.title: The Angelus
02-28.line: the angel of the Lord declared unto Mary.
02-28.meaning: for centuries, church bells rang at morning, noon and evening for this short prayer. pause at noon today.

02-29.title: Psalm 121
02-29.line: I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from whence help shall come to me.
02-29.meaning: look up today. help is closer than it feels.

03-01.title: St. Benedict
03-01.line: let all guests be received as Christ.
03-01.meaning: Benedict's monks still welcome visitors this way. who will you welcome today?

03-02.title: Micah 6
03-02.line: do judgment, and love mercy, and walk solicitous with thy God.
03-02.meaning: three simple things: be fair, be kind, walk with God.

03-03.title: St. Katharine Drexel
03-03.line: she gave away a fortune to start schools for those left out.
03-03.meaning: an heiress from Philadelphia who became a sister and founded schools for Black and Native American children. what we have is meant to be shared.

03-04.title: St. Casimir
03-04.line: a prince who chose prayer and the poor.
03-04.meaning: a young Polish prince who loved Mary and lived simply. kindness looks good on anyone.

03-05.title: Anima Christi
03-05.meaning: an old prayer often said after Communion. a short line to carry all day.

03-06.title: Luke 10
03-06.line: Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and art troubled about many things.
03-06.meaning: Jesus said this gently. one thing is needed: to sit with him a moment.

03-07.title: Sts. Perpetua and Felicity
03-07.line: stand fast in the faith, and love one another.
03-07.meaning: a young mother and her servant, martyred together in Carthage in 203. her own diary survives.
03-07.source: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity 20 (paraphrase)

03-08.title: St. John of God
03-08.line: he cared for the sick and the poor of Granada with his own hands.
03-08.meaning: his order, the Brothers Hospitallers, still serves in hospitals today. care for one person is never small.

03-09.title: St. Frances of Rome
03-09.line: a wife and mother who prayed and served the poor of Rome.
03-09.meaning: Frances often left her prayers to help her family, and said she found God there too. home is holy ground.

03-10.title: St. Augustine
03-10.line: love, and do what you will.
03-10.meaning: if love is the root, the rest grows well.
03-10.source: Augustine, Homily 7 on the First Letter of John (paraphrase)

03-11.title: Psalm 139
03-11.line: I will praise thee, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
03-11.meaning: you were made with care. so was everyone you'll meet today.
03-11.source: Psalm 138:14 (Douay-Rheims, paraphrase; Psalm 139:14 in other Bibles)

03-12.title: Matthew 6
03-12.line: consider the lilies of the field, how they grow.
03-12.meaning: the flowers don't worry, and they are cared for. so are you.

03-13.title: St. Thomas More
03-13.line: pray for me, as I will for thee, that we may merrily meet in heaven.
03-13.meaning: written to his daughter from prison. faith and cheer, side by side.
03-13.source: Thomas More, letter to Margaret Roper, 1535

03-14.title: Act of Hope
03-14.line: O my God, relying on thy promises, I hope.
03-14.meaning: hope isn't wishful thinking. it leans on God's promises.

03-15.title: Isaiah 40
03-15.line: they that hope in the Lord shall renew their strength.
03-15.meaning: tired? that's okay. strength comes back.

03-16.title: St. Francis of Assisi
03-16.line: praised be you, my Lord, through Sister Water.
03-16.meaning: Francis saw water as a sister: useful, humble, precious, pure. bless a glass of water today.
03-16.source: Francis of Assisi, Canticle of the Creatures

03-17.title: St. Patrick
03-17.line: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me.
03-17.meaning: once a captive in Ireland, Patrick went back to bring the faith to the people who held him. say this line on your way out the door.
03-17.source: St. Patrick's Breastplate, traditional (C. F. Alexander's translation)

03-18.title: St. Cyril of Jerusalem
03-18.line: he taught new Christians, one lesson at a time.
03-18.meaning: Cyril's lectures for people preparing for baptism still survive. faith grows by steady, simple teaching.
03-18.source: Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lectures; optional memorial

03-19.title: St. Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary
03-19.line: Joseph did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him.
03-19.meaning: not one word of Joseph is recorded in the Gospels, only what he did. quiet faithfulness counts.

03-20.title: Luke 15
03-20.line: this my son was dead, and is come to life again.
03-20.meaning: the father in the parable ran to meet his son. God runs toward us too.

03-21.title: Come, Holy Spirit
03-21.line: come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.
03-21.meaning: a short prayer before work, study or a hard talk.
03-21.source: traditional prayer to the Holy Spirit

03-22.title: John 6
03-22.line: I am the bread of life.
03-22.meaning: Catholics hear this at every Mass. what feeds your soul today?

03-23.title: St. Turibius of Mogrovejo
03-23.line: a bishop who walked the Andes to visit his people.
03-23.meaning: he learned local languages and defended the dignity of native peoples in Peru. showing up is a way of loving.

03-24.title: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
03-24.line: I will spend my heaven doing good on earth.
03-24.meaning: the Little Flower promised to keep helping. saints are friends who still care.

03-25.title: The Annunciation of the Lord
03-25.line: behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word.
03-25.meaning: Mary's yes changed everything. what small yes could you say today?

03-26.title: Psalm 34
03-26.line: taste, and see that the Lord is sweet.
03-26.meaning: faith isn't only an idea. it can be tasted, lived, enjoyed.

03-27.title: Mark 4
03-27.meaning: Jesus said it to the storm, and it calmed. say it to your own storm today.

03-28.title: St. Gregory the Great
03-28.line: the proof of love is in the works.
03-28.meaning: love shows itself in what we do.
03-28.source: Gregory the Great, Homilies on the Gospels 30 (paraphrase)

03-29.title: The Memorare
03-29.line: remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known.
03-29.meaning: an old prayer of trust: no one who asked Mary's help was left alone.

03-30.title: Proverbs 3
03-30.line: have confidence in the Lord with all thy heart.
03-30.meaning: you don't have to figure everything out today.

03-31.title: St. Ignatius of Loyola
03-31.line: love ought to show itself in deeds more than in words.
03-31.meaning: a short, practical test for any day.

04-01.title: Matthew 18
04-01.line: where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I.
04-01.meaning: faith is shared. a short prayer with one other person counts.

04-02.title: St. Francis of Paola
04-02.line: a hermit whose motto was one word: charity.
04-02.meaning: he founded the Minims, who lived very simply. love is the whole of it.

04-03.title: Psalm 103
04-03.line: bless the Lord, O my soul.
04-03.meaning: begin with thanks. it changes how the rest of the day looks.

04-04.title: St. Isidore of Seville
04-04.line: he tried to gather all that was known into one book.
04-04.meaning: a bishop and scholar of Spain who wrote an early encyclopedia. learning can be a gift to others.
04-04.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

04-05.title: St. Vincent Ferrer
04-05.line: a preacher who crossed Europe on foot calling people to peace.
04-05.meaning: a Dominican of Valencia who preached in town after town. a kind word travels far.

04-06.title: St. Teresa of Calcutta
04-06.line: the fruit of silence is prayer; the fruit of prayer is faith.
04-06.meaning: her little path from quiet to love. start with one minute of silence.

04-07.title: St. John Baptist de la Salle
04-07.line: he gave his life to teaching poor children.
04-07.meaning: the founder of the Christian Brothers, patron of teachers. thank a teacher today.

04-08.title: Salve Regina
04-08.line: hail, holy Queen, mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope.
04-08.meaning: monks sing this at the end of the day. a tender prayer for tired hearts.

04-09.title: John 13
04-09.line: a new commandment I give unto you: that you love one another.
04-09.meaning: the whole Gospel in one line.

04-10.title: St. Basil the Great
04-10.line: the bread you keep belongs to the hungry.
04-10.meaning: Basil reminded the rich of his city that what we hold is meant to be shared.
04-10.source: Basil the Great, Homily on Luke 12:18 (paraphrase)

04-11.title: St. Stanislaus
04-11.line: a bishop of Kraków who spoke up and paid with his life.
04-11.meaning: Stanislaus is a patron of Poland. courage often begins with a quiet conscience.

04-12.title: Psalm 27
04-12.line: the Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear?
04-12.meaning: light in the dark. carry it today.

04-13.title: St. Martin I
04-13.line: a pope who stayed faithful in exile.
04-13.meaning: Martin I died far from Rome, true to what he believed. faith can stand even when everything else is taken.

04-14.title: Romans 12
04-14.line: rejoice with them that rejoice; weep with them that weep.
04-14.meaning: being with people where they are is love.

04-15.title: St. Teresa of Ávila
04-15.line: God walks among the pots and pans.
04-15.meaning: Teresa told her sisters God is in kitchen work too. ordinary tasks can be holy.
04-15.source: Teresa of Ávila, Book of the Foundations 5 (paraphrase)

04-16.title: Prayer before meals
04-16.line: bless us, O Lord, and these thy gifts.
04-16.meaning: a simple grace. say it before your next meal, even quietly.

04-17.title: Isaiah 49
04-17.line: I will not forget thee. Behold, I have graven thee in my hands.
04-17.meaning: God's love is like a mother's, and even stronger.

04-18.title: St. Francis de Sales
04-18.line: nothing is so strong as gentleness, nothing so gentle as real strength.
04-18.meaning: gentleness isn't weak. try it in one hard moment today.

04-19.title: Luke 6
04-19.line: be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
04-19.meaning: God's mercy is the model for ours.

04-20.title: Psalm 131
04-20.line: I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother.
04-20.meaning: rest like a child in God's lap today.
04-20.source: Psalm 130:2 (Douay-Rheims, paraphrase; Psalm 131:2 in other Bibles)

04-21.title: St. Anselm
04-21.meaning: Anselm, a monk and archbishop of Canterbury, believed faith loves to ask questions. bring yours to God today.

04-22.title: St. John of the Cross
04-22.line: where there is no love, put love, and you will find love.
04-22.meaning: if a place feels cold, bring warmth. it comes back.
04-22.source: John of the Cross, letter to Mother María de la Encarnación, 1591 (paraphrase)

04-23.title: St. George
04-23.line: a soldier martyr, honored across East and West.
04-23.meaning: George's story became a tale of courage against a dragon. every day has a fear we can face with God.
04-23.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; also St. Adalbert

04-24.title: St. Fidelis of Sigmaringen
04-24.line: a lawyer who became a friar to serve those with no defender.
04-24.meaning: Fidelis was known as the poor man's lawyer. use what you're good at for someone who needs it.

04-25.title: St. Mark, Evangelist
04-25.line: go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature.
04-25.meaning: Mark wrote the shortest Gospel, full of action. share one good thing you have heard today.

04-26.title: Act of Love
04-26.line: O my God, I love thee above all things.
04-26.meaning: a short, strong prayer for the morning.

04-27.title: 1 John 4
04-27.line: God is charity: and he that abideth in charity, abideth in God.

04-28.title: St. Louis de Montfort
04-28.meaning: a French preacher who loved the poor and wrote about trust in Mary. also St. Peter Chanel, martyr of the Pacific, today.
04-28.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorials; motto associated with his True Devotion

04-29.title: St. Catherine of Siena
04-29.line: if you are what you should be, you will set the whole world on fire.
04-29.meaning: a Doctor of the Church who never went to school and still advised popes. be fully yourself today.

04-30.title: St. Pius V
04-30.line: a Dominican pope who lived simply.
04-30.meaning: tradition says he kept his white Dominican habit, and popes have worn white since. small habits can last centuries.

05-01.title: St. Joseph the Worker
05-01.line: is not this the carpenter's son?
05-01.meaning: Jesus grew up in a working home. whatever your work is today, it can be offered to God.

05-02.title: St. Athanasius
05-02.line: God became man so that we might share in his life.
05-02.meaning: a bishop of Alexandria who defended the faith in Christ's divinity, often from exile. faith is a gift worth guarding.

05-03.title: Sts. Philip and James, Apostles
05-03.line: Lord, shew us the Father, and it is enough for us.
05-03.meaning: Philip asked an honest question and Jesus answered: whoever sees me sees the Father.

05-04.title: Matthew 7
05-04.line: ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find.
05-04.meaning: God likes being asked. ask today.

05-05.title: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
05-05.line: love seeks no cause beyond itself.
05-05.meaning: God's love isn't earned. it simply is.
05-05.source: Bernard of Clairvaux, Sermons on the Song of Songs 83 (paraphrase)

05-06.title: Psalm 90
05-06.line: teach us to number our days, that we may gain a wise heart.
05-06.meaning: each day counts. this one too.
05-06.source: Psalm 89:12 (Douay-Rheims, paraphrase; Psalm 90:12 in other Bibles)

05-07.title: Prayer to the guardian angel
05-07.line: angel of God, my guardian dear.
05-07.meaning: a prayer many learned as children. it's still true.

05-08.title: John 10
05-08.meaning: a shepherd knows each sheep by name. so does he.

05-09.title: St. Augustine
05-09.line: God loves each of us as if there were only one of us to love.
05-09.meaning: you are not lost in the crowd.

05-10.title: St. Damien of Molokai
05-10.line: he went to live among those everyone else had sent away.
05-10.meaning: a Belgian priest who served the leprosy colony in Hawaii and caught the disease himself. love comes close.
05-10.source: U.S. calendar, optional memorial; also St. John of Ávila

05-11.title: Psalm 63
05-11.line: O God, my God, to thee do I watch at break of day.
05-11.meaning: an old morning prayer. give God the first thought of the day.

05-12.title: Sts. Nereus, Achilleus and Pancras
05-12.line: early Roman martyrs, remembered for steady courage.
05-12.meaning: Nereus and Achilleus were soldiers; Pancras was a teenager. faith is not about age or rank.

05-13.title: Our Lady of Fatima
05-13.meaning: in 1917 Mary appeared to three shepherd children in Portugal asking for prayer and peace. one decade today is a fine start.

05-14.title: St. Matthias, Apostle
05-14.meaning: chosen to take Judas's place, Matthias had followed Jesus quietly all along. faithful presence gets noticed.

05-15.title: St. Isidore the Farmer
05-15.line: a farmer who prayed while he plowed.
05-15.meaning: Isidore and his wife Maria shared their food with anyone hungry. patron of farmers and rural life.

05-16.title: 2 Corinthians 12
05-16.line: my grace is sufficient for thee: for power is made perfect in infirmity.
05-16.meaning: weakness is not a dead end. it's where grace works.

05-17.title: St. Catherine of Siena
05-17.line: all the way to heaven is heaven.
05-17.meaning: the journey itself can hold God's joy.

05-18.title: St. John I
05-18.line: a pope who died a prisoner for the sake of the Church.
05-18.meaning: John I traveled to Constantinople on a hard mission and died after returning. faithfulness is not always rewarded here.

05-19.title: The Magnificat
05-19.line: he hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble.
05-19.meaning: Mary's song turns the world upside down, in favor of the small.

05-20.title: St. Bernardine of Siena
05-20.line: he carried a tablet with the name of Jesus to every town.
05-20.meaning: a Franciscan preacher who spread devotion to the Holy Name. keep his name near today.

05-21.title: St. Christopher Magallanes and Companions
05-21.line: priests and lay people of Mexico who stayed faithful in a hard time.
05-21.meaning: Christopher Magallanes forgave his executioners. forgiveness takes great strength.

05-22.title: St. Rita of Cascia
05-22.meaning: a wife, mother, widow and nun who made peace between feuding families. no situation is beyond hope.

05-23.title: Psalm 4
05-23.line: in peace in the selfsame I will sleep, and I will rest.
05-23.meaning: a good line for tonight. you can let today go.

05-24.title: Galatians 6
05-24.meaning: who could use a hand today?

05-25.title: St. Bede the Venerable
05-25.line: a monk who wrote the history of the English Church.
05-25.meaning: Bede spent his whole life in one monastery, studying, teaching and singing. a small world can hold a deep life.
05-25.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; also Sts. Gregory VII and Mary Magdalene de Pazzi

05-26.title: St. Philip Neri
05-26.line: a joyful heart is more easily made perfect.
05-26.meaning: the cheerful saint of Rome, famous for his jokes and his kindness. holiness can laugh.

05-27.title: St. Augustine of Canterbury
05-27.line: sent to England with forty monks, he began with kindness.
05-27.meaning: Pope Gregory sent him, and he became the first archbishop of Canterbury. some of the best things begin as a nervous journey.

05-28.title: Ecclesiastes 3
05-28.meaning: if today is a waiting season, it is still a season.

05-29.title: St. Paul VI
05-29.line: the pope who saw the Second Vatican Council through to its end.
05-29.meaning: Paul VI was the first pope to fly to other continents. he went to meet people where they were.

05-30.title: Prayer of St. Francis
05-30.line: Lord, make me an instrument of your peace.
05-30.meaning: this prayer dates from about 1912, in the spirit of Francis. where can you bring peace today?

05-31.title: The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
05-31.line: my soul doth magnify the Lord.
05-31.meaning: Mary hurried to help her cousin Elizabeth, and joy broke out. visit or call someone today.

06-01.title: St. Justin Martyr
06-01.line: on Sunday we all gather together in one place.
06-01.meaning: around the year 150, Justin described the Mass to outsiders. it still looks much the same.

06-02.title: Sts. Marcellinus and Peter
06-02.line: a priest and an exorcist of Rome, martyred together.
06-02.meaning: their names are in the Roman Canon of the Mass. the Church never forgets its faithful.

06-03.title: St. Charles Lwanga and Companions
06-03.line: young martyrs of Uganda who stood firm together.
06-03.meaning: Charles Lwanga protected the young pages in his care. faith can make the young brave.

06-04.title: Psalm 42
06-04.line: as the hart panteth after the fountains of water; so my soul panteth after thee.
06-04.meaning: that thirst you feel is for God.

06-05.title: St. Boniface
06-05.meaning: an English monk who brought the faith to the Germans and was martyred in old age. a long journey of faith ends at home with God.

06-06.title: St. Norbert
06-06.line: a rich courtier who turned to God after a near miss in a storm.
06-06.meaning: Norbert founded the Premonstratensians. a scare can become a turning point.

06-07.title: St. Gregory of Nyssa
06-07.line: the one who keeps climbing never stops beginning.
06-07.meaning: growth in God never ends. every day is a new start.
06-07.source: Gregory of Nyssa, Homilies on the Song of Songs 8 (paraphrase)

06-08.title: James 1
06-08.line: let every man be swift to hear, but slow to speak.

06-09.title: St. Ephrem
06-09.line: the harp of the Holy Spirit.
06-09.meaning: a deacon of Syria who taught the faith through hymns. songs teach hearts what words alone cannot.
06-09.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

06-10.title: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
06-10.line: to pick up a pin for love can save a soul.
06-10.meaning: tiny acts done with love are never wasted.

06-11.title: St. Barnabas, Apostle
06-11.line: Barnabas, which is, by interpretation, the son of consolation.
06-11.meaning: Barnabas vouched for Paul when others were afraid of him. be someone's encourager today.

06-12.title: Eternal rest
06-12.line: may perpetual light shine upon them.
06-12.meaning: pray once today for someone you've lost.

06-13.title: St. Anthony of Padua
06-13.meaning: a Franciscan preacher whose words drew crowds. many still ask his help finding what is lost, including peace.
06-13.source: General Roman Calendar, memorial; Doctor of the Church

06-14.title: Psalm 100
06-14.line: sing joyfully to God, all the earth.
06-14.meaning: a little song is a prayer.

06-15.title: Luke 18
06-15.line: O God, be merciful to me a sinner.
06-15.meaning: the honest prayer Jesus praised. short and true.

06-16.title: St. Ambrose
06-16.line: no duty is more urgent than that of returning thanks.

06-17.title: Psalm 91
06-17.line: he will overshadow thee with his shoulders: and under his wings thou shalt trust.
06-17.meaning: imagine being sheltered like a bird under wings.

06-18.title: The Our Father
06-18.line: thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
06-18.meaning: the hardest and freest line in the prayer.

06-19.title: St. Romuald
06-19.line: sit in your cell as in paradise.
06-19.meaning: the founder of the Camaldolese hermits. find a few quiet minutes today and let them be enough.

06-20.title: Colossians 3
06-20.line: above all these things have charity, which is the bond of perfection.

06-21.title: St. Aloysius Gonzaga
06-21.line: a young Jesuit who died caring for the sick in Rome.
06-21.meaning: Aloysius gave up a noble title and died at 23 serving plague victims. patron of young people.

06-22.title: Sts. John Fisher and Thomas More
06-22.line: the king's good servant, but God's first.
06-22.meaning: Thomas More's reported last words. both men kept their conscience at great cost. also St. Paulinus of Nola today.
06-22.source: Thomas More, reported words on the scaffold, 1535

06-23.title: St. Francis of Assisi
06-23.line: praised be you, my Lord, through our Sister, Mother Earth.
06-23.meaning: Francis saw the earth as sister and mother who feeds us. walk gently today.
06-23.source: Francis of Assisi, Canticle of the Creatures

06-24.title: The Nativity of St. John the Baptist
06-24.line: he must increase, but I must decrease.
06-24.meaning: John pointed away from himself to Jesus. being small can be freeing.

06-25.title: John 20
06-25.meaning: the first words of the risen Jesus to his friends. he says them to you.

06-26.title: Psalm 145
06-26.line: the Lord is sweet to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.

06-27.title: St. Cyril of Alexandria
06-27.line: he defended the title of Mary as Mother of God.
06-27.meaning: Cyril was a key voice at the Council of Ephesus in 431. who Jesus is matters.
06-27.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

06-28.title: St. Irenaeus
06-28.line: the glory of God is a human being fully alive.
06-28.meaning: a bishop of Lyon who learned from Polycarp. God delights when you flourish.

06-29.title: Sts. Peter and Paul, Apostles
06-29.line: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
06-29.meaning: a fisherman and a scholar, very different men, both pillars of the Church in Rome.

06-30.title: The First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church
06-30.line: the unnamed Christians of Rome who died under Nero.
06-30.meaning: we don't know their names, but God does. faithfulness doesn't need to be famous.

07-01.title: St. Junípero Serra
07-01.line: always go forward, never turn back.
07-01.meaning: a Franciscan who walked the California missions despite a painful leg. his motto, 'siempre adelante', kept him going.
07-01.source: U.S. calendar, optional memorial; his motto

07-02.title: St. Ignatius of Loyola
07-02.line: pray as if everything depends on God; work as if everything depends on you.
07-02.meaning: a classic summary of his teaching. trust and effort go together.
07-02.source: traditional saying in the spirit of Ignatius

07-03.title: St. Thomas, Apostle
07-03.meaning: Thomas doubted, then said the clearest words of faith in the Gospels. doubt can lead somewhere good.

07-04.title: St. Elizabeth of Portugal
07-04.line: a queen who made peace in her own family.
07-04.meaning: Elizabeth calmed quarrels between her husband and son, and cared for the poor. peacemaking starts at home.
07-04.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial (U.S.: July 5)

07-05.title: St. Anthony Zaccaria
07-05.line: a doctor who became a priest to heal souls too.
07-05.meaning: he founded the Barnabites and loved the letters of St. Paul. read a few lines of Paul today.

07-06.title: St. Maria Goretti
07-06.line: she forgave the one who hurt her.
07-06.meaning: an Italian girl of 11 who forgave her attacker before she died. he later repented and attended her canonization.

07-07.title: Te Deum
07-07.line: we praise thee, O God: we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.
07-07.meaning: an ancient hymn of thanks. sung on big days, but any day can be one.

07-08.title: Matthew 5
07-08.line: you are the light of the world.

07-09.title: St. Augustine Zhao Rong and Companions
07-09.line: the martyrs of China, faithful over three centuries.
07-09.meaning: 120 men, women and children of faith, honored together. faith has deep roots in every land.

07-10.title: Psalm 16
07-10.line: thou hast made known to me the ways of life.
07-10.meaning: God shows the path a step at a time.

07-11.title: St. Benedict
07-11.line: listen with the ear of your heart.
07-11.meaning: the father of Western monks wrote a short Rule full of balance and kindness. listen today before you speak.

07-12.title: St. Clare of Assisi
07-12.line: go forth in peace, for you have followed the good road.
07-12.meaning: Clare's last words. a blessing for anyone on the way.

07-13.title: St. Henry
07-13.line: an emperor who tried to rule with faith.
07-13.meaning: Henry II supported monasteries and the Church in Germany. power can be used to serve.

07-14.title: St. Kateri Tekakwitha
07-14.meaning: a young Mohawk and Algonquin woman who prayed in the woods and cared for others. the first Native American saint.

07-15.title: St. Bonaventure
07-15.line: a Franciscan who wrote of the soul's journey to God.
07-15.meaning: Bonaventure taught that all creation is a ladder to God. look at one beautiful thing today and say thank you.
07-15.source: Bonaventure, The Journey of the Mind into God (summary); memorial

07-16.title: Our Lady of Mount Carmel
07-16.meaning: the Carmelites, who began as hermits on Mount Carmel, honor Mary today. many wear the brown scapular as a sign of trust.

07-17.title: Romans 12
07-17.line: be not overcome by evil, but overcome evil by good.
07-17.meaning: answer one hard thing today with something good.

07-18.title: Isaiah 55
07-18.line: my thoughts are not your thoughts: nor your ways my ways.
07-18.meaning: God sees farther than we do. that can be a relief.

07-19.title: Isaiah 6
07-19.line: lo, here am I, send me.
07-19.meaning: Isaiah said yes before he knew the task. a willing heart is enough to start.

07-20.title: St. Apollinaris
07-20.meaning: his church in Ravenna still shines with old mosaics. the faith has been beautiful for a long time.

07-21.title: St. Lawrence of Brindisi
07-21.line: a Capuchin friar who spoke many languages.
07-21.meaning: he preached across Europe and is a Doctor of the Church. a gift for words can be a gift for peace.

07-22.title: St. Mary Magdalene
07-22.meaning: the risen Jesus called her by name, and she became the first to tell the others. she is called the apostle to the apostles.

07-23.title: St. Bridget of Sweden
07-23.line: a mother of eight who became a mystic and founder.
07-23.meaning: Bridget founded the Bridgettines and is a patron of Europe. every season of life can hold God.

07-24.title: St. Sharbel Makhluf
07-24.line: a Lebanese hermit who lived in deep prayer.
07-24.meaning: Sharbel spent 23 years as a hermit in the mountains of Lebanon. silence can be full of God.

07-25.title: St. James, Apostle
07-25.line: can you drink the chalice that I shall drink?
07-25.meaning: James said yes, and was the first apostle to die for Christ. pilgrims still walk the Camino to his shrine in Spain.

07-26.title: Sts. Joachim and Anne
07-26.meaning: tradition names them as Mary's parents. call or remember your grandparents today.

07-27.title: Nunc dimittis
07-27.line: now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace.
07-27.meaning: Simeon's evening prayer, said every night in the Church's night prayer.

07-28.title: Psalm 37
07-28.line: commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him.
07-28.meaning: hand today over. you don't carry it alone.

07-29.title: Sts. Martha, Mary and Lazarus
07-29.line: I have believed that thou art Christ the Son of the living God.
07-29.meaning: Martha said this while grieving her brother. Jesus loved to visit their home in Bethany.

07-30.title: St. Peter Chrysologus
07-30.line: golden words, as his name means.
07-30.meaning: a bishop of Ravenna known for short, clear sermons. say something kind and brief today.
07-30.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

07-31.title: St. Ignatius of Loyola
07-31.meaning: a wounded soldier who read the lives of saints while recovering, and founded the Jesuits. God can be found in today, exactly as it is.

08-01.title: St. Alphonsus Liguori
08-01.meaning: a lawyer turned bishop who wrote simple books on prayer for ordinary people. prayer is the great means.
08-01.source: Alphonsus Liguori, The Great Means of Salvation (paraphrase)

08-02.title: St. Peter Julian Eymard
08-02.line: he taught people to spend time with Christ in the Eucharist.
08-02.meaning: the founder of the Blessed Sacrament priests. also St. Eusebius of Vercelli today. a few minutes in a quiet church can be a gift.

08-03.title: Hebrews 13
08-03.line: Jesus Christ, yesterday, and today; and the same for ever.

08-04.title: St. John Vianney
08-04.line: prayer is nothing else than union with God.
08-04.meaning: the Curé of Ars, a parish priest who spent hours hearing confessions. patron of parish priests: pray for yours.

08-05.title: The Dedication of the Basilica of St. Mary Major
08-05.line: the oldest church in the West dedicated to Mary.
08-05.meaning: built in Rome after the Council of Ephesus. a legend says snow fell there in August.

08-06.title: The Transfiguration of the Lord
08-06.line: this is my most beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him.
08-06.meaning: on the mountain the disciples saw Jesus in glory before the hard road ahead. hold on to bright moments.

08-07.title: St. Cajetan
08-07.line: a priest who trusted God for every need.
08-07.meaning: Cajetan founded the Theatines and is patron of work and job seekers in many places. also St. Sixtus II and companions today.

08-08.title: St. Dominic
08-08.line: to contemplate, and to give to others the fruits of contemplation.
08-08.meaning: the founder of the Order of Preachers. what you learn in prayer is meant to be shared.
08-08.source: Dominican motto, from Thomas Aquinas, Summa II-II, q.188, a.6

08-09.title: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
08-09.line: whoever seeks the truth is seeking God, whether they know it or not.
08-09.meaning: Edith Stein, a philosopher of Jewish birth who became a Carmelite, killed at Auschwitz in 1942. a patron of Europe.

08-10.title: St. Lawrence, deacon and martyr
08-10.line: the poor are the treasures of the Church.
08-10.meaning: asked to hand over the Church's treasures, Lawrence gathered the poor of Rome.
08-10.source: Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy II.28 (paraphrase)

08-11.title: St. Clare
08-11.line: gaze upon him, consider him, contemplate him.
08-11.meaning: Clare followed Francis and founded the Poor Clares. simply looking with love is a prayer.
08-11.source: Clare of Assisi, Second Letter to Agnes of Prague (paraphrase)

08-12.title: St. Jane Frances de Chantal
08-12.line: a widow who founded an order for women of every age and health.
08-12.meaning: Jane and Francis de Sales were great friends in faith. good friendships help us grow.

08-13.title: Sts. Pontian and Hippolytus
08-13.line: a pope and a priest who had disagreed, reconciled in exile.
08-13.meaning: both were sent to the mines of Sardinia and died there. differences can end in peace.

08-14.title: St. Maximilian Kolbe
08-14.line: greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
08-14.meaning: in Auschwitz, Kolbe offered his life in place of a father of a family. love can be stronger than anything.

08-15.title: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
08-15.line: he that is mighty hath done great things to me.
08-15.meaning: Mary was taken body and soul into heaven. God's promise holds for the whole person, body too.

08-16.title: St. Stephen of Hungary
08-16.line: a king who wrote to his son: be merciful.
08-16.meaning: Stephen helped bring the faith to Hungary and urged his son to be kind and patient. advice worth passing on.
08-16.source: Stephen of Hungary, Admonitions to his son (paraphrase); optional memorial

08-17.title: Ruth 1
08-17.line: whithersoever thou shalt go, I will go.
08-17.meaning: Ruth's promise to Naomi. loyalty is a quiet kind of love.

08-18.title: Luke 24
08-18.line: stay with us, because it is towards evening.
08-18.meaning: the disciples at Emmaus begged Jesus to stay. you can ask the same.

08-19.title: St. John Eudes
08-19.line: he spread love for the hearts of Jesus and Mary.
08-19.meaning: a French priest who served plague victims and founded communities for women in need.

08-20.title: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
08-20.line: the measure of loving God is to love without measure.
08-20.meaning: a Cistercian abbot whose words on love still warm hearts. there's no limit on love today.
08-20.source: Bernard of Clairvaux, On Loving God 1 (paraphrase)

08-21.title: St. Pius X
08-21.line: to restore all things in Christ.
08-21.meaning: a parish priest who became pope and opened Holy Communion to children. his motto came from St. Paul.
08-21.source: motto of Pius X, from Ephesians 1:10

08-22.title: The Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary
08-22.line: a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun.
08-22.meaning: a week after the Assumption, the Church honors Mary as queen. her crown is her humility.

08-23.title: St. Rose of Lima
08-23.line: the first saint of the Americas.
08-23.meaning: Rose lived simply in her family home in Lima and cared for the poor and sick there. holiness at home.

08-24.title: St. Bartholomew, Apostle
08-24.meaning: Philip said this to Bartholomew (Nathanael), who doubted anything good came from Nazareth. invite, don't argue.

08-25.title: St. Louis of France
08-25.line: a king who fed the poor at his own table.
08-25.meaning: Louis IX was known for justice and charity. also St. Joseph Calasanz, founder of free schools, today.

08-26.title: Psalm 119
08-26.line: thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths.
08-26.meaning: enough light for the next step.

08-27.title: St. Monica
08-27.line: the son of these tears cannot perish.
08-27.meaning: Monica prayed for years for her son Augustine. a bishop told her this. keep praying for the people you love.

08-28.title: St. Augustine
08-28.line: late have I loved you, beauty so ancient and so new.
08-28.meaning: after a restless youth Augustine found God, who had been inside him all along. it's never too late.

08-29.title: The Passion of St. John the Baptist
08-29.line: John spoke the truth, even to a king.
08-29.meaning: John the Baptist was imprisoned and put to death by Herod. truth spoken with love is brave.

08-30.title: St. Augustine
08-30.meaning: a well-known saying in Augustine's spirit. sing something today.

08-31.title: Prayer for peace
08-31.meaning: an old Latin prayer, 'da pacem Domine'. for your home and the world.

09-01.title: 1 Thessalonians 5
09-01.meaning: not constant words. a heart turned toward God, all day.

09-02.title: Psalm 130
09-02.line: out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord.
09-02.meaning: you can pray from any low place.

09-03.title: St. Gregory the Great
09-03.line: servant of the servants of God.
09-03.meaning: a monk who became pope, he chose this humble title. leadership is service.
09-03.source: title used by Gregory the Great

09-04.title: St. Bonaventure
09-04.line: all creation is a mirror that shows God.
09-04.meaning: look closely at one created thing today.
09-04.source: Bonaventure, The Journey of the Mind into God 1 (paraphrase)

09-05.title: St. Teresa of Calcutta
09-05.line: do small things with great love.
09-05.meaning: Mother Teresa served the poorest in Calcutta. the size of the task matters less than the love in it.
09-05.source: attributed to Teresa of Calcutta (paraphrase); feast day Sept. 5

09-06.title: Matthew 6
09-06.line: where thy treasure is, there is thy heart also.
09-06.meaning: what we love most shapes us. choose well.

09-07.title: John 8
09-07.line: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me walketh not in darkness.
09-07.meaning: even dim days have light in them.

09-08.title: The Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
09-08.meaning: nine months after the Immaculate Conception, the Church celebrates her birth. a happy day to say thank you for mothers.

09-09.title: St. Peter Claver
09-09.meaning: a Jesuit in Cartagena who met slave ships and cared for the people on them. love goes to the wounded first.
09-09.source: Peter Claver's own vow (paraphrase); U.S. memorial

09-10.title: Dante Alighieri
09-10.line: in his will is our peace.
09-10.meaning: the great Catholic poet put it simply: trusting God lets the heart rest.

09-11.title: Act of Faith
09-11.line: O my God, I firmly believe.
09-11.meaning: faith is said aloud sometimes, to steady the heart.

09-12.title: The Most Holy Name of Mary
09-12.meaning: a name is a person. say hers gently today, and ask her to pray for you.

09-13.title: St. John Chrysostom
09-13.line: honor Christ in the poor at the church door, not only at the altar.
09-13.meaning: John the golden-mouthed preached that worship and care for the poor belong together.

09-14.title: The Exaltation of the Holy Cross
09-14.line: God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son.
09-14.meaning: the cross is not only suffering: it is love that would not stop.

09-15.title: Our Lady of Sorrows
09-15.line: thy own soul a sword shall pierce.
09-15.meaning: Mary stood near the cross. she knows grief, and stays near those who suffer.

09-16.title: Sts. Cornelius and Cyprian
09-16.line: a pope and a bishop who stood together for unity.
09-16.meaning: they welcomed back those who had fallen away in persecution. mercy and unity go together.

09-17.title: St. Robert Bellarmine
09-17.line: a Jesuit scholar who wrote a simple catechism for children.
09-17.meaning: the great debater also loved teaching kids. clear and simple can be the deepest. St. Hildegard of Bingen is also remembered on this day.
09-17.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

09-18.title: Psalm 133
09-18.line: behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
09-18.meaning: peace at home is a quiet miracle.

09-19.title: St. Januarius
09-19.line: a bishop of Naples and martyr.
09-19.meaning: Naples still gathers to pray at his relic each year. faith runs deep in a city's heart.

09-20.title: Sts. Andrew Kim Tae-gon, Paul Chong Ha-sang and Companions
09-20.meaning: the faith came to Korea through lay people reading books. Andrew Kim was the first Korean priest.

09-21.title: St. Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist
09-21.line: follow me. And he arose up and followed him.
09-21.meaning: a tax collector, disliked by many, who left his table to follow Jesus. no one is past being called.

09-22.title: St. Thomas Aquinas
09-22.line: the things we love tell us what we are.
09-22.meaning: look at what you love today. it says a lot.

09-23.title: St. Pius of Pietrelcina
09-23.meaning: Padre Pio, a Capuchin priest who heard confessions for hours each day. his famous advice still fits.

09-24.title: Philippians 4
09-24.line: whatsoever things are lovely, think on these things.
09-24.meaning: choose one lovely thing to think about.

09-25.title: Psalm 150
09-25.line: let every spirit praise the Lord.
09-25.meaning: the last line of the Psalms is pure praise.

09-26.title: Sts. Cosmas and Damian
09-26.line: twin doctors who cared for the sick without charge.
09-26.meaning: they are in the Roman Canon of the Mass. a gift freely given is beautiful.

09-27.title: St. Vincent de Paul
09-27.line: he organized charity so the poor would be served well.
09-27.meaning: Vincent and Louise de Marillac founded the Daughters of Charity. kindness grows when it has a plan.

09-28.title: St. Wenceslaus
09-28.meaning: the Christmas carol about him was written much later. also St. Lawrence Ruiz, first Filipino saint, today.

09-29.title: Sts. Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels
09-29.meaning: that is what the name Michael means. Gabriel brings good news, Raphael heals and guides travelers.
09-29.source: meaning of the name Michael; feast

09-30.title: St. Jerome
09-30.line: ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.
09-30.meaning: Jerome translated the Bible into Latin. read one verse slowly today.

10-01.title: St. Thérèse of the Child Jesus
10-01.meaning: the Little Flower found her place in the Church: to love, in small ways, every day.
10-01.source: Thérèse of Lisieux, Story of a Soul, ch. 9 (paraphrase)

10-02.title: The Holy Guardian Angels
10-02.line: he hath given his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
10-02.meaning: you are not walking alone today.

10-03.title: Psalm 37
10-03.line: delight in the Lord, and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.
10-03.meaning: what you most deeply want, bring it to God.

10-04.title: St. Francis of Assisi
10-04.line: praised be you, my Lord, through Brother Sun.
10-04.meaning: Francis sang to God through all creation. step outside for a minute today and notice something alive.
10-04.source: Francis of Assisi, Canticle of the Creatures

10-05.title: St. Faustina Kowalska
10-05.meaning: a Polish sister who wrote of God's mercy in her diary. five words to carry all day.

10-06.title: St. Bruno
10-06.line: the founder of the Carthusians, who live in silence.
10-06.meaning: Bruno left a teaching post to pray in the mountains. some of the best words are unsaid.

10-07.title: Our Lady of the Rosary
10-07.line: hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
10-07.meaning: the rosary walks through Jesus's life with Mary. one Hail Mary slowly is a good start.

10-08.title: Prayer to St. Michael
10-08.line: St. Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle.
10-08.meaning: a short prayer for protection, prayed after Mass for many years.
10-08.source: Prayer to St. Michael, Leo XIII

10-09.title: St. Denis and Companions
10-09.line: the first bishop of Paris, martyred with two companions.
10-09.meaning: Denis is a patron of France. also St. John Leonardi, a pharmacist turned priest, today.

10-10.title: John 21
10-10.meaning: Jesus gave Peter a job after he had failed. love gets a second chance.

10-11.title: St. John XXIII
10-11.line: see everything, overlook a great deal, correct a little.
10-11.meaning: the warm-hearted pope who opened the Second Vatican Council. a gentle rule for any home.
10-11.source: attributed to John XXIII; optional memorial

10-12.title: Psalm 8
10-12.line: what is man that thou art mindful of him?
10-12.meaning: small under the stars, and still remembered.

10-13.title: Matthew 7
10-13.line: by their fruits you shall know them.
10-13.meaning: let what you do today say who you are.

10-14.title: St. Callistus I
10-14.line: a former slave who became pope.
10-14.meaning: Callistus was known for welcoming sinners back with mercy. your past is not your end.

10-15.title: St. Teresa of Ávila
10-15.line: let nothing disturb you; God alone is enough.
10-15.meaning: a Carmelite reformer full of humor and fire. say her prayer once when the day gets busy.

10-16.title: St. Margaret Mary Alacoque
10-16.line: she spread love of the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
10-16.meaning: a Visitation sister in France. the heart of God is open. also St. Hedwig today.

10-17.title: St. Ignatius of Antioch
10-17.line: I am the wheat of God.
10-17.meaning: on his way to martyrdom in Rome, Ignatius wrote letters to the churches. they still speak of unity and courage.
10-17.source: Ignatius of Antioch, Letter to the Romans 4

10-18.title: St. Luke, Evangelist
10-18.meaning: Luke wrote a Gospel full of mercy: the prodigal son, the good Samaritan. read one of his stories today.

10-19.title: Sts. John de Brébeuf, Isaac Jogues and Companions
10-19.meaning: French Jesuits and lay helpers who lived among the Huron and Mohawk peoples. love crossed oceans.

10-20.title: St. Paul of the Cross
10-20.meaning: Paul taught that Christ's love is shown most of all on the cross. love that stays is the deepest kind.

10-21.title: Wisdom 11
10-21.line: thou lovest all things that are, and hatest none of the things which thou hast made.
10-21.meaning: from the Book of Wisdom. everything that exists is loved into being.

10-22.title: St. John Paul II
10-22.line: do not be afraid! open wide the doors for Christ.
10-22.meaning: his first words as pope in 1978. a good line to say before anything new today.
10-22.source: John Paul II, homily at the start of his pontificate, Oct. 22, 1978

10-23.title: St. John of Capistrano
10-23.line: a lawyer and governor who became a Franciscan preacher.
10-23.meaning: he traveled all over Europe preaching hope. it's never too late to change paths.

10-24.title: St. Anthony Mary Claret
10-24.line: a weaver's son who became a missionary bishop.
10-24.meaning: Anthony Claret founded the Claretians and preached across Spain and Cuba. small beginnings, big heart.

10-25.title: St. Teresa of Ávila
10-25.line: the important thing is not to think much, but to love much.
10-25.meaning: love more than you think today.
10-25.source: Teresa of Ávila, Interior Castle IV.1 (paraphrase)

10-26.title: Tobit 4
10-26.line: what thou hatest to be done to thee by another, see thou never do to another.
10-26.meaning: an old form of the golden rule, from the Book of Tobit.

10-27.title: Psalm 95
10-27.line: come, let us praise the Lord with joy.
10-27.meaning: the psalm that opens the Church's daily prayer.

10-28.title: Sts. Simon and Jude, Apostles
10-28.meaning: we know little of them, but they followed Jesus to the end. Jude is the patron of hopeless causes.

10-29.title: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
10-29.meaning: said near the end of her short life. even today's small things carry a gift.
10-29.source: Thérèse of Lisieux, Last Conversations, June 5, 1897 (paraphrase)

10-30.title: The Our Father
10-30.line: forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
10-30.meaning: forgiveness flows both ways. is there one small thing to let go today?

10-31.title: Sirach 2
10-31.line: you that fear the Lord, hope in him.
10-31.meaning: hope is a choice you can make again today.

11-01.title: All Saints
11-01.line: a great multitude, which no man could number.
11-01.meaning: not just famous saints: every ordinary person now with God. who do you remember today?

11-02.title: All Souls
11-02.line: eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord.
11-02.meaning: today the Church prays for everyone who has died. say a name you miss.

11-03.title: St. Martin de Porres
11-03.line: a Dominican brother of Lima who cared for everyone.
11-03.meaning: the son of a Spanish noble and a freed woman of Panama, he cared for the sick, the poor and even animals.

11-04.title: St. Charles Borromeo
11-04.line: a young cardinal who helped renew the Church.
11-04.meaning: Charles started seminaries and cared for the sick in plague time in Milan. renewal begins with care.

11-05.title: Psalm 84
11-05.line: better is one day in thy courts above thousands.
11-05.meaning: a little time with God is never wasted.

11-06.title: St. Francis de Sales
11-06.line: half an hour of prayer a day is essential, except when busy; then an hour.
11-06.meaning: a playful saying in his spirit: the busier the day, the more we need prayer.
11-06.source: traditional saying attributed to Francis de Sales

11-07.title: Luke 2
11-07.line: glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men of good will.
11-07.meaning: the angels' song. it's not just for Christmas.

11-08.title: Matthew 28
11-08.line: behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world.

11-09.title: The Dedication of the Lateran Basilica
11-09.line: the mother church of Rome and the world.
11-09.meaning: the pope's cathedral, not St. Peter's, is the Lateran. every church building says: God lives with his people.

11-10.title: St. Leo the Great
11-10.meaning: a pope who stood calmly before Attila. remember who you are today: loved.
11-10.source: Leo the Great, Sermon 21 on the Nativity (paraphrase)

11-11.title: St. Martin of Tours
11-11.line: he cut his cloak in two for a beggar.
11-11.meaning: Martin was a young soldier when he shared his cloak. that night, the story says, he dreamed Christ wore it.
11-11.source: Sulpicius Severus, Life of St. Martin 3 (summary)

11-12.title: St. Josaphat
11-12.line: a bishop who gave his life for Christian unity.
11-12.meaning: an Eastern Catholic archbishop in what is now Belarus. unity is worth great cost.

11-13.title: St. Frances Xavier Cabrini
11-13.line: the first U.S. citizen to be canonized.
11-13.meaning: Mother Cabrini founded schools, orphanages and hospitals for immigrants. she crossed the ocean many times, though she feared water.

11-14.title: St. John Bosco
11-14.line: run, jump, shout, but do not sin.
11-14.meaning: Don Bosco loved to see kids play. joy and holiness are friends.

11-15.title: St. Albert the Great
11-15.meaning: the teacher of Thomas Aquinas, Albert studied plants, animals and stars. curiosity about creation can be prayer.
11-15.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

11-16.title: St. Margaret of Scotland
11-16.line: a queen who fed the poor before she ate.
11-16.meaning: Margaret served orphans and the poor at her own table. also St. Gertrude the Great today.

11-17.title: St. Elizabeth of Hungary
11-17.line: a young princess who built a hospital for the poor.
11-17.meaning: Elizabeth died at 24 after giving her life to the sick. youth is time enough for great love.

11-18.title: The Dedication of the Basilicas of Sts. Peter and Paul
11-18.line: two great churches over two great apostles.
11-18.meaning: Peter's basilica and Paul's outside the walls in Rome. also St. Rose Philippine Duchesne in the U.S. today.

11-19.title: Psalm 62
11-19.line: only in God is my soul at rest.
11-19.source: Psalm 61:2 (Douay-Rheims, paraphrase; Psalm 62:1 in other Bibles)

11-20.title: Isaiah 9
11-20.line: the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.

11-21.title: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
11-21.line: Mary, offered to God from childhood.
11-21.meaning: an old tradition says Mary was brought to the Temple as a child. offer God the start of anything new.

11-22.title: St. Cecilia
11-22.line: she sang in her heart to the Lord.
11-22.meaning: a Roman martyr and patron of musicians. hum a hymn today, even quietly.

11-23.title: St. Clement I
11-23.line: an early pope who wrote a letter calling for peace.
11-23.meaning: his letter to Corinth asked a divided church to choose humility. also St. Columban, Irish missionary, today.

11-24.title: St. Andrew Dung-Lac and Companions
11-24.meaning: 117 priests and lay people who stayed faithful through long persecution. strength in quiet steadiness.

11-25.title: St. Catherine of Alexandria
11-25.line: a wise young woman who argued for her faith.
11-25.meaning: Catherine is a patron of students and philosophers. thinking hard is a way of honoring God.

11-26.title: St. Ephrem
11-26.line: the Word of God is a tree of life that offers blessed fruit on every side.
11-26.meaning: come back to Scripture again and again: there's always more.

11-28.title: Psalm 147
11-28.line: he healeth the broken of heart, and bindeth up their bruises.
11-28.meaning: a broken heart is held tenderly by God.

11-29.title: St. Teresa of Calcutta
11-29.meaning: a simple place to start today.

11-30.title: St. Andrew, Apostle
11-30.meaning: Andrew's first move was to bring his brother Peter. who could you bring to something good?

12-01.title: John 11
12-01.line: I am the resurrection and the life.
12-01.meaning: Jesus said this to grieving Martha. death never gets the last word.

12-02.title: Psalm 136
12-02.line: praise ye the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
12-02.meaning: the psalm repeats it 26 times. some things are worth repeating.

12-03.title: St. Francis Xavier
12-03.line: a missionary who sailed to India and Japan.
12-03.meaning: Francis Xavier, friend of Ignatius, gave his life to sharing the faith in Asia. patron of missions.

12-04.title: St. John Damascene
12-04.line: he defended holy images and wrote beautiful hymns.
12-04.meaning: a monk near Jerusalem, a Doctor of the Church. beauty can lead the heart to God.

12-05.title: St. Hildegard of Bingen
12-05.line: the earth is full of green life from God.
12-05.meaning: Hildegard spoke of viriditas, God's greening power in all living things.

12-06.title: St. Nicholas
12-06.line: a bishop famous for secret gifts.
12-06.meaning: the real Nicholas of Myra quietly helped families in need. the best gifts don't need credit.

12-07.title: St. Ambrose
12-07.meaning: Ambrose was chosen bishop of Milan by the crowd before he was even baptized. God calls in surprising ways.
12-07.source: General Roman Calendar, memorial; Doctor of the Church

12-08.title: The Immaculate Conception
12-08.meaning: from the first moment of her life, Mary was kept free from sin by God's grace. grace goes before us too.
12-08.source: Luke 1:28 (Douay-Rheims); patronal feast of the U.S.

12-09.title: St. Juan Diego
12-09.line: am I not here, I who am your mother?
12-09.meaning: the words Mary spoke to Juan Diego, a humble man of Mexico, at Tepeyac in 1531.

12-10.title: Matthew 19
12-10.line: suffer the little children, and forbid them not to come to me.
12-10.meaning: Jesus made time for children. make time for one today.

12-11.title: St. Damasus I
12-11.line: a pope who asked Jerome to translate the Bible.
12-11.meaning: because of him, the Latin Vulgate was made. good work often starts with one request.

12-12.title: Our Lady of Guadalupe
12-12.line: let not your heart be troubled.
12-12.meaning: Mary appeared to Juan Diego as a mother of the people of the Americas. her image still hangs in Mexico City.
12-12.source: Nican Mopohua (paraphrase); feast in the U.S.

12-13.title: St. Lucy
12-13.meaning: a young martyr of Syracuse, remembered in the darkest weeks of the year with candles and songs.

12-14.title: St. John of the Cross
12-14.line: in the evening of life, we will be judged on love.
12-14.meaning: a Carmelite poet who wrote of the dark night of the soul. love is the measure.
12-14.source: John of the Cross, Sayings of Light and Love 64 (paraphrase)

12-15.title: Psalm 34
12-15.line: the Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart.
12-15.meaning: if you're hurting, God is close.

12-16.title: St. Anthony of Padua
12-16.line: actions speak louder than words; let your words teach and your actions speak.
12-16.meaning: a line from his sermons. let today's deeds do the talking.

12-17.title: 1 Peter 5
12-17.line: casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you.

12-18.title: Psalm 19
12-18.line: the heavens shew forth the glory of God.

12-19.title: St. Vincent de Paul
12-19.line: go to the poor: you will find God.
12-19.meaning: Vincent saw Christ in every person in need.

12-20.title: Luke 11
12-20.meaning: the disciples asked, and Jesus gave them the Our Father. you can ask too.

12-21.title: St. Peter Canisius
12-21.line: a Jesuit who wrote catechisms in plain words.
12-21.meaning: Peter Canisius taught the faith across Germany. clear teaching is a gift.
12-21.source: General Roman Calendar, optional memorial; Doctor of the Church

12-22.title: Isaiah 30
12-22.line: in silence and in hope shall your strength be.
12-22.meaning: quiet trust is a kind of strength.

12-23.title: St. John of Kanty
12-23.line: a professor who never turned away a poor person.
12-23.meaning: a teacher in Kraków known for giving away his own clothes and food. learning and kindness belong together.

12-24.title: Christmas Eve
12-24.line: there was no room for them in the inn.
12-24.meaning: tonight the Church waits by the manger. make a little room in your heart.

12-25.title: The Nativity of the Lord
12-25.line: today is born to you a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord.
12-25.meaning: merry Christmas. God came as a child, small enough to hold.

12-26.title: St. Stephen, the first martyr
12-26.line: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.
12-26.meaning: the day after Christmas, the Church remembers Stephen, who forgave even as he died.

12-27.title: St. John, Apostle and Evangelist
12-27.meaning: in old age, John is said to have repeated this again and again. it was enough.

12-28.title: The Holy Innocents
12-28.line: a voice in Rama was heard, lamentation and great mourning.
12-28.meaning: the children of Bethlehem killed by Herod. today we hold every child who suffers in prayer.

12-29.title: St. Thomas Becket
12-29.line: an archbishop who chose God over the king's favor.
12-29.meaning: Thomas was killed in Canterbury Cathedral in 1170. conscience is worth keeping.

12-30.title: St. Gregory Nazianzen
12-30.line: remember God more often than you breathe.

12-31.title: St. Sylvester I
12-31.line: the pope at the end of the age of persecution.
12-31.meaning: Sylvester led the Church in Rome when Christians could finally worship openly. give thanks for this year.

2026-11-22.title: Christ the King
2026-11-22.line: my kingdom is not of this world.
2026-11-22.meaning: the last Sunday of the church year. a king who serves and washes feet.

2026-11-29.title: First Sunday of Advent
2026-11-29.line: watch ye therefore, for you know not when the lord of the house cometh.
2026-11-29.meaning: a new church year begins. light the first candle and wait with hope.

2026-12-06.title: Second Sunday of Advent
2026-12-06.line: prepare ye the way of the Lord.
2026-12-06.meaning: John the Baptist's call. clear one small path for God this week.

2026-12-13.title: Gaudete Sunday
2026-12-13.meaning: the third Sunday of Advent: the rose candle. joy is near.

2026-12-20.title: Fourth Sunday of Advent
2026-12-20.line: behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel.
2026-12-20.meaning: Emmanuel means God with us. almost Christmas.

2026-12-27.title: The Holy Family
2026-12-27.line: and the child grew, and waxed strong, full of wisdom.
2026-12-27.meaning: Jesus grew up in a real family. bless your own household today.

2027-01-03.title: The Epiphany of the Lord
2027-01-03.line: we have seen his star in the east, and are come to adore him.
2027-01-03.meaning: in the U.S. the Epiphany is kept today. what gift could you bring?

2027-01-06.title: St. André Bessette
2027-01-06.line: a humble doorkeeper who welcomed thousands.
2027-01-06.meaning: Brother André of Montreal opened the door, listened and prayed with everyone. a small job done with love.

2027-01-10.title: The Baptism of the Lord
2027-01-10.line: thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.
2027-01-10.meaning: the Christmas season ends here. your baptism means you are beloved too.

2027-02-10.title: Ash Wednesday
2027-02-10.line: remember, man, that thou art dust, and unto dust thou shalt return.
2027-02-10.meaning: Lent begins. forty days to come back to God with prayer, fasting and giving.
2027-02-10.source: Genesis 3:19; words at the giving of ashes

2027-02-14.title: First Sunday of Lent
2027-02-14.line: Jesus was led by the spirit into the desert.
2027-02-14.meaning: Jesus spent forty days in the desert. Lent is our forty days.

2027-03-07.title: Laetare Sunday
2027-03-07.meaning: halfway through Lent, the Church wears rose and takes a breath of joy.

2027-03-21.title: Palm Sunday
2027-03-21.line: hosanna to the son of David: blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
2027-03-21.meaning: Holy Week begins. walk with Jesus this week.

2027-03-25.title: Holy Thursday
2027-03-25.line: do this for a commemoration of me.
2027-03-25.meaning: the Last Supper and the washing of feet. tonight the Church keeps watch.

2027-03-26.title: Good Friday
2027-03-26.line: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.
2027-03-26.meaning: the day Jesus died on the cross. a day of quiet, fasting and love.

2027-03-27.title: Holy Saturday
2027-03-27.meaning: the Church waits at the tomb. tonight the Easter Vigil lights the new fire.
2027-03-27.source: from an ancient Holy Saturday homily (Office of Readings)

2027-03-28.title: Easter Sunday
2027-03-28.line: he is not here, for he is risen, as he said.
2027-03-28.meaning: Christ is risen. alleluia! the greatest feast of the year.

2027-03-29.title: Easter Monday
2027-03-29.line: this is the day which the Lord hath made.
2027-03-29.meaning: Easter lasts eight days as one great day. keep the joy going.
2027-03-29.source: Psalm 117:24 (Douay-Rheims), sung through the Easter octave

2027-04-04.title: Divine Mercy Sunday
2027-04-04.meaning: the end of the Easter octave, a day to trust God's mercy.
2027-04-04.source: Second Sunday of Easter; Faustina Kowalska, Diary

2027-04-05.title: The Annunciation of the Lord
2027-04-05.line: fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace with God.
2027-04-05.meaning: moved from March 25 this year because of Holy Week. Mary's yes, celebrated in Easter light.

2027-05-06.title: The Ascension of the Lord
2027-05-06.line: why stand you looking up to heaven?
2027-05-06.meaning: Jesus returns to the Father. in many U.S. dioceses this is kept on Sunday, May 9.

2027-05-09.title: Seventh Sunday of Easter
2027-05-09.line: that they all may be one.
2027-05-09.meaning: Jesus prayed for his friends to be one. in many U.S. dioceses, the Ascension is celebrated today.

2027-05-16.title: Pentecost
2027-05-16.line: they were all filled with the Holy Ghost.
2027-05-16.meaning: the Spirit came like wind and fire, and the Church was born. ask for the Spirit today.

2027-05-17.title: Mary, Mother of the Church
2027-05-17.meaning: from the cross Jesus gave Mary to John, and to us.

2027-05-23.title: The Most Holy Trinity
2027-05-23.line: in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.
2027-05-23.meaning: one God, three persons, a communion of love. we begin every prayer here.

2027-05-30.title: The Body and Blood of Christ
2027-05-30.meaning: Corpus Christi: the gift of the Eucharist. in the U.S. kept today; elsewhere on Thursday, May 27.

2027-06-04.title: The Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
2027-06-04.line: learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart.
2027-06-04.meaning: the heart of Jesus is gentle. rest in it today.

2027-06-05.title: The Immaculate Heart of Mary
2027-06-05.line: his mother kept all these words in her heart.
2027-06-05.meaning: the day after the Sacred Heart, we honor Mary's heart.

2027-11-21.title: Christ the King
2027-11-21.line: Lord, remember me when thou shalt come into thy kingdom.
2027-11-21.meaning: the thief's prayer on the cross, answered with paradise. the church year ends with mercy.

2027-11-28.title: First Sunday of Advent
2027-11-28.line: it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep.
2027-11-28.meaning: a new church year begins. wake up to hope.

2027-12-05.title: Second Sunday of Advent
2027-12-05.meaning: God makes a way through the low places.

2027-12-12.title: Gaudete Sunday
2027-12-12.meaning: the rose candle: joy is near. Our Lady of Guadalupe is also close to our hearts today.

2027-12-19.title: Fourth Sunday of Advent
2027-12-19.line: blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
2027-12-19.meaning: Elizabeth's greeting to Mary. Christmas is days away.

2027-12-26.title: The Holy Family
2027-12-26.line: he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.
2027-12-26.meaning: ordinary family life, holy. Christmas joy continues.
